 Medium
 Large
 1 / 10 ​Exclusive: Abhijeet Sawant recalls struggles after winning Indian Idol; says, ‘I faced criticism and people's taunts, there was pressure to achieve big things'
 Abhijeet Sawant, who became a household name after winning the debut season of Indian Idol has now returned to the same platform for a new season. During an exclusive conversation with Times of India TV, the singer opened up about his journey over the years and his struggling phase. He also shared how his victory became a source of hope for middle-class families. Abhijeet recalled the tough phase after winning Indian Idol when he had to face criticism and listen to people's taunts. (Photo: Instagram)
 2 / 10 ​When we started our journey with Indian Idol, there was a lot of negativity around reality shows
 At the same time, I felt proud of how much talent the show has produced over the years and how many talented singers it has introduced to the industry. When we started our journey with Indian Idol, there was a lot of negativity around the format of reality shows. People questioned whether it was really producing talented singers and giving them opportunities or whether their success would last only for a short time. (Photo: Instagram)
 3 / 10 ​When I returned to the stage, it felt like coming back home after achieving something meaningful
 Honestly, I have faced such criticism the most, and I still do because I represent that platform. When I returned to the stage, it felt like coming back home after achieving something meaningful over the years. It was a wonderful feeling, almost like being the eldest member of the family, sharing my blessings with everyone. (Photo: Instagram)
 4 / 10 ​This was the right time to bring the show back and reunite all of us
 This is the perfect time for the show to return. If it had come a little earlier or later, I don't know how things would have turned out, but I feel this is the right time. Today, you can see several stars who started their journeys with Indian Idol and other reality shows appearing on television again. Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi had a season 2. I am part of this show, while Rahul Vaidya is doing another show. Many others are also reuniting. There has also been a viral trend on social media featuring pictures from the 1980s and 1990s. I think this was the right time to bring the show back and reunite all of us on the same platform. (Photo: Instagram)
 5 / 10 ​My dreams were quite limited, but after winning Indian Idol, they became bigger
 I never imagined that I would see myself on television. I always thought I would perform at shows and make music. My dreams were quite limited, but after winning Indian Idol, they became bigger. I started dreaming of becoming a playback singer, entering the pop music industry and making a name for myself. Even today, when I look at my car and house, I never imagined that I would live this kind of life. Every artist has a different background, and many have someone who supports them and encourages them to dream big. They have family members or mentors who tell them that they can achieve great things. However, I had no family background in the industry, and nobody was supporting me in pursuing this profession. (Photo: Instagram)
 6 / 10 ​People from my own family never imagined that I could become a big star
 People from my own family never imagined that I could become a big star. I began dreaming of all these things, and I received the support I needed because of Indian Idol. When I stood on that stage again and looked back at what I had achieved, I realised how much we are capable of doing. There is still so much to achieve in life. Of course, there are disappointments and things that remain unfinished, but I have also achieved a lot. Even today, it means a great deal when people remember you. This is especially true for singers because their songs often remind people of certain moments, situations or individuals in their lives. But when people see a singer or an artist, they can relive those memories. That is something rare. (Photo: Instagram)
 7 / 10 I was not just a winner. I'd become a source of hope for many middle-class families
 Someone once shared a memory of watching the Indian Idol finale with his mother when I won the competition. His mother told him, ‘Look, this boy has won. Now good things will happen in our lives too.’ When he shared this with me, I realised that I was not just a winner or a contestant on a reality show. I had become a source of hope for many middle-class families who believed that they, too, could achieve something in life. Today, we have social media, and everyone is doing their own thing. But back then, things were very different. I could not fully understand the impact I had made all those years ago. Now, I am able to look back and understand it much better. (Photo: Instagram)
 8 / 10 ​People started expecting me to achieve something big
 A lot of hard work goes into building a career. For example, when we see an actor or a star, they may be working only for themselves, and whatever opportunities they get are for their own growth. That was my situation before the show. However, when star kids enter the industry, they already have the responsibility of living up to their parents' success. They are expected to become as successful as their parents, and that pressure is enormous. I faced a similar kind of pressure after winning Indian Idol. People started expecting me to achieve something big, and managing those expectations while focusing on my work was a major challenge. (Photo: Instagram)
 9 / 10 ​I had to face criticism, listen to people's taunts and read negative comments about myself in newspapers
 At least star kids have a family background in the industry. I had no such background, and my parents came from a humble background too. There was nothing at home that could guide or prepare me for the future I was stepping into. Despite that, I had to face criticism, listen to people's taunts and read negative articles about myself in newspapers. There was also the constant question of what a reality show winner could actually achieve. Over the years, I have become stronger and learned how to handle such situations. That is the biggest lesson I have taken away from this journey. (Photo: Instagram)
 10 / 10 ​Abhijeet recalls his struggling phase
 During our time, the industry was very restrictive, which made things difficult. Everything was already established; singers and music directors already had their own place in the industry. We had to approach people and ask for work, but they were not very open to giving opportunities to reality show contestants. People felt insecure because we, the reality show contestants, had become so popular that we were bigger than many playback singers. (Photo: Instagram)
